title: Log Aggregation for Distributed Microservices
business: A retail logistics company operating a fleet of distributed microservices across multiple compute environments.
problem: The engineering team struggles to correlate errors across fragmented service logs, leading to extended mean-time-to-resolution during intermittent order processing failures.
solution: By centralizing application logs into Amazon CloudWatch Logs, the team gains a unified interface to query and analyze log streams, allowing for cross-service pattern matching and centralized retention management.
steps: Install the CloudWatch agent on compute instances to capture local application log files.
Configure log groups to define retention policies for compliance and data lifecycle management.
Define log streams within log groups to organize data by specific service instances or containers.
Utilize CloudWatch Logs Insights to execute queries across multiple log groups for rapid error identification.
Set up subscription filters to route specific error patterns to downstream notification services.
outcome: Engineers achieve a holistic view of the request lifecycle, enabling faster identification of root causes without manual log file aggregation.
limitation: CloudWatch Logs imposes a maximum limit on the size of individual log events; if an application generates exceptionally large stack traces, the log ingestion may be truncated, which can be checked by monitoring the IngestionError metric.
